key_insight: SpecGP is a transformer-based model conditioned on collision energy that predicts N-glycopeptide fragment spectra with enhanced ion coverage, enabling energy-adaptable spectral forecasts and improving isomer discrimination via rescoring.
problem_solved: Existing spectral predictors struggle to model glycopeptide fragmentation across different collision energies and provide limited fragment coverage, hindering accurate isomer identification and confident peptide–glycan assignment.
method: Transformer sequence-to-spectrum model that conditions predictions on collision energy to produce energy-adaptable spectra.
Architecture and training strategies that explicitly enhance fragment-ion coverage for glycan- and peptide-derived ions (glycan-specific cleavages included).
Use predicted spectra for rescoring experimental identifications, boosting isomer discrimination and overall identification confidence.
impact: Shows how conditional transformer models can incorporate experimental variables (collision energy) to improve predictive mass-spectrometry tasks; provides a practical ML workflow for better identification and rescoring in glycoproteomics and related proteomic applications.
visual_elements: Schematic of the SpecGP transformer architecture with an energy-conditioning input node
Overlayed spectral plots (predicted vs. observed) across low/medium/high collision energies to show energy-adaptability
Bar/ROC chart comparing identification/rescoring performance and isomer discrimination before vs. after SpecGP rescoring
Illustration of a glycopeptide and annotated fragment ions highlighting improved fragment coverage
paper_title: SpecGP as a transformer-based model for predicting energy-adaptable structural spectra of glycopeptides
paper_authors: Xianyong Wang, Rui Song, Zhuangzhuang Feng, Shisheng Sun
